page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c4.4xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs utilizing an Intel Xeon 8369HB processor clocked at 3.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The hardware configuration includes 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a compute-focused ratio of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. No local storage or GPU accelerators are bundled with this instance type, and it delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 6 Gbps.

In benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates consistent mid-tier performance. The Intel Xeon processor achieves a stress-ng single-core score of 1578.98 and a multi-core score of 16657.34, supported by advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and vector neural network instructions (AVX512_VNNI, AVX512_BF16). Memory performance shows a distinct contrast: while cached small-block read bandwidth reaches 921.81 GB/sec, uncached large-block write bandwidth drops to 50.62 GB/sec, and the PassMark memory score is positioned in the bottom 25% at 1797.16.

For database and web workloads, the ecs.c4.4xlarge handles 15.83 million Redis SET operations per second and achieves a static web serving throughput of 9.51 GB/sec. Small-scale language model inference is viable, with a 135M parameter model processing prompts at 991.37 tokens per second, though performance drops significantly on larger 7B models. This hardware profile is qualitatively cost-efficient for compute-heavy, memory-light workloads such as web serving, batch processing, and lightweight serialization tasks, whereas memory-bound databases may experience bottlenecks.

Benchmark data indicates average CPU capabilities, with a PassMark CPU score of 17360.29 and support for AVX-512 vector instructions. The instance is well-suited for compute-intensive workloads such as static web serving, which registers at 9.51 GB/sec, Redis caching operations, and lightweight machine learning inference, though it is less optimal for memory-heavy database applications.
